fields.title: Neuroblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuroblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Neuroblastoma is a type of cancer that most often affects young children. It arises in nerve tissue, particularly in the area of the adrenal glands or around the spinal cord in the chest or abdomen. In Israel, patients with neuroblastoma have access to a comprehensive approach to treatment combining innovative diagnostic methods, advanced treatment strategies and rehabilitation support.

Diagnosis of neuroblastoma

  1. Physical examination and history
    Includes assessment of the symptoms and gathering information about the child's medical history.
  2. Laboratory tests
    Blood and urine tests for markers characteristic of neuroblastoma, including catecholamine levels.
  3. Ultrasound scan
    Helps detect a tumour in the area of the adrenal glands or in the abdominal cavity.
  4. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods for establishing the size and position of the tumour and how far it has spread.
  5. PET-CT
    Assessment of the metabolic activity of the tumour and detection of metastases.
  6. Biopsy
    Obtaining and analysing a sample of tumour tissue to confirm the diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatment of neuroblastoma

  1. Surgery
    Aimed at removing as much of the tumour as possible without harming the child's health.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to shrink the tumour before surgery and to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells locally, particularly where the tumour cannot be removed completely by surgery.
  4. High-dose chemotherapy followed by a stem cell transplant
    A method used to treat widespread neuroblastoma.
  5. Immunotherapy
    The newest treatment strategy, aimed at activating the child's immune system to fight the tumour.
  6. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Leading specialists in oncology, surgery, radiology and paediatrics work together to develop the most effective treatment plan.
  • Individualised treatment: Treatment strategies are developed taking account of every aspect of the child's health and the particular features of the illness.
  • Access to the newest technology and medicines: The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, including clinical trials of new medicines.
  • Support and rehabilitation: Comprehensive support for the child and family at every stage of treatment, including rehabilitation programmes.

Treatment of neuroblastoma in Israel combines highly qualified specialists, advanced treatments and a deep understanding of the need to support young patients and their families, offering strong prospects of recovery and a return to full life.

fields.title: Neuroendocrine cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuroendocrine cancer (NEC) is a rare and complex cancer arising from the cells of the neuroendocrine system, which have both nerve and endocrine functions. These tumours can arise in any organ, but occur most often in the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas and the lungs. Israel has developed advanced methods of diagnosing and treating this condition, which makes it possible to achieve good results and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of neuroendocrine cancer

  1. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood and urine tests to identify specific markers such as chromogranin A and 5-HIAA, which help establish the presence and activity of the tumour.
  2. Somatostatin receptor PET-CT:
    • Positron emission tomography (PET) combined with computed tomography (CT), using radiopharmaceuticals that bind to somatostatin receptors. This allows tumours and metastases to be imaged precisely, giving a high level of diagnostic accuracy.
  3. Biopsy:
    • A biopsy of the tumour followed by histological and immunohistochemical analysis to confirm the diagnosis and establish the type of neuroendocrine tumour. The biopsy helps determine the exact nature of the tumour and choose the best treatment.

Treatments for neuroendocrine cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Tumour resection: removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue. Used in localised forms of the disease.
    • Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and cryoablation: minimally invasive methods used to destroy the tumour with high or low temperatures.
  2. Drug treatment:
    • Biotherapy: the use of somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide), which suppress hormone secretion and slow the growth of the tumour.
    • Targeted therapy: the use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour cells (sunitinib, everolimus).
    • Chemotherapy: prescribed in aggressive forms of NEC or where the cancer has spread.
  3. Radiotherapy:
    • Local radiotherapy: used to shrink the tumour and relieve symptoms.
    • Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT): an innovative treatment in which radionuclides bind to the tumour cells through somatostatin receptors and destroy them from within.
  4. Radioembolisation:
    • Introduction of radioactive microspheres into the blood vessels supplying the tumour, which reduces its size and activity.

Advantages of treating neuroendocrine cancer in Israel:

  1. Highly qualified specialists: internationally recognised oncologists with extensive experience in treating rare and complex cancers.
  2. Modern equipment: the use of the newest technology and devices for accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach: personalised treatment regimens developed with each patient's particular circumstances in mind.
  4. Innovative treatments: the use of advanced therapies such as PRRT and targeted therapy.
  5. High standards of quality: compliance with international protocols and standards for cancer treatment.
  6. Comprehensive support: a multidisciplinary approach involving oncologists, surgeons, radiologists, endocrinologists and other specialists to provide patients with all-round care.

Treatment of neuroendocrine cancer in Israel achieves good results and improves both the outlook and quality of life for patients, thanks to modern methods of diagnosis and therapy and the professionalism of Israeli doctors.

fields.title: Diabetes insipidus
fields.bodyHtml:
Diabetes insipidus: approaches to treatment in Israel

Diabetes insipidus is a rare condition in which the balance of fluid in the body is disturbed. It is caused by a lack of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or by that hormone not working effectively, which leads to excessive loss of water in the urine. In Israel, patients with diabetes insipidus are offered a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

Diagnosis of diabetes insipidus:

  1. History and physical examination
    The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as excessive thirst and frequent urination, and carries out a general medical examination.
  2. Urine test
    Helps establish the concentration of the urine, which is usually low in patients with diabetes insipidus.
  3. Blood tests for electrolytes and kidney function
    Allow assessment of sodium and other electrolyte levels and of how the kidneys are working.
  4. Water deprivation test
    The patient is asked to go without fluids for a set period while doctors monitor changes in the volume of urine passed and in electrolyte concentrations.
  5. MRI of the brain
    May be ordered to rule out other causes, such as tumours, that can produce symptoms resembling diabetes insipidus.

Treatment of diabetes insipidus in Israel:

  1. Replacement therapy
    Administration of a synthetic analogue of ADH, such as desmopressin, to control the symptoms of the condition.
  2. Lifestyle adjustments
    Advice on maintaining hydration and on changes to the diet to manage symptoms.
  3. Treatment of the underlying condition
    Where the diabetes insipidus is caused by another condition, such as a pituitary tumour, treating it may require surgery or other therapy.
  4. Monitoring and support
    Regular monitoring of electrolyte levels and kidney function, together with support from medical staff to ensure the condition is managed properly.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach
    Treatment is chosen according to the features of each case and any accompanying conditions.
  • Access to the newest medicines
    The use of the most modern medicines, including desmopressin in various forms (tablets, nasal spray, injections), for effective control of symptoms.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists
    Close cooperation between endocrinologists, neurologists, surgeons and other specialists for a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Educational programmes for patients
    Information and support for patients and their families to help them understand the condition and how to control it.

Treatment of diabetes insipidus in Israel aims to minimise symptoms, prevent complications and improve patients' quality of life, with a comprehensive and joined-up approach to managing the condition.

fields.title: Ulcerative colitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Ulcerative colitis: advanced treatment in Israel

Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterised by periods of flare-up and remission. Israel uses modern methods of diagnosing and treating this condition, aimed at reducing symptoms and achieving lasting remission.

Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis:

  1. Colonoscopy with biopsy:
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the inner surface of the large bowel to be examined and tissue samples to be taken for histological examination.
  2. Barium enema:
    An X-ray examination of the bowel using a contrast medium to assess changes in the structure of the bowel.
  3. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood tests: full blood count, markers of inflammation (C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate).
    • Stool tests: for occult blood and calprotectin (a marker of inflammation in the bowel).

Treatments for ulcerative colitis:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Aminosalicylates (mesalazine): used to reduce inflammation and maintain remission.
    • Corticosteroids: used to control acute flare-ups.
    • Immunosuppressants (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine): to reduce the immune response and maintain remission.
    • Biological medicines (infliximab, adalimumab): targeted therapies for moderate and severe ulcerative colitis.
  2. Surgery:
    • Carried out where drug treatment is ineffective or serious complications develop (massive bleeding or perforation of the bowel, for example).
    • Proctocolectomy with ileoanal anastomosis: removal of the affected section of bowel followed by restoration of function.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: a personal treatment plan based on thorough investigation and on the particular features of each patient's illness.
  • Multidisciplinary teams: gastroenterologists, surgeons, dietitians and psychologists working together for a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Access to advanced treatments: the use of advanced treatments, including biological medicines and targeted therapy, which considerably improve both the outlook and patients' quality of life.
  • Personalised support: support for patients at every stage of treatment, from diagnosis through to recovery and rehabilitation.
  • Thorough support during remission: planning of diet and medication and regular medical check-ups to maintain health and prevent relapse.

Treatment of ulcerative colitis in Israel aims to achieve lasting remission and a considerable improvement in patients' quality of life, giving them access to the most effective and modern treatments.
